text:
sam_sales: Hey team — QuantHealth POC wants EU-only data residency + subprocessor list asap. Also asking for a routing policy that keeps requests in eu-west-1 unless failover. They care about latency (<=120ms p95) and BYOK for keys. Any blockers on Dedicated or Private for this?
lena_se: Nice, thanks Sam. Quick Qs: 1) Do they need control-plane in EU too or just data plane? 2) Are they ok with cross-border control signals for metrics?
priya_privacy: They said 'control plane can be global but audit logs + encryption keys must remain in EU.' Need to confirm HSM/BYO KMS options and subprocessor attestation.
marco_eng: For runtime: we can pin tenant to eu-west-1 pool and configure regional failover to eu-central-1. Batching behavior may affect p95 under 120ms — need workload profile.
sam_sales: They expect bursty inference (up to 300 rps) with median seq len ~256 tokens. Also asked about egress cost modeling per-region.
omar_ops: For Dedicated, reserved capacity quote handles baseline. Burst pricing for extra capacity is separate. Egress: we bill per-GB by region, send detailed numbers in pricing sheet.
lena_se: Also they asked for subprocessor list filtered to EU-only. We have some non-EU monitoring endpoints — is that a blocker?
marco_eng: We send telemetry to vendor X (US) by default for aggregated metrics. We can disable that for Private/Dedicated and route metrics to an EU endpoint (requires enabling EU telemetry toggle and legal attestation).
priya_privacy: Legal will need an attestation template. I can pull the subprocessor inventory and redact non-EU ones, but customer will likely request a signed addendum for BYOK + no egress.
sam_sales: Customer wants a representative SOW with explicit routing policy: data_in_region -> eu-west-1; control_plane_signals -> allowed to global but masked; failover -> eu-central-1 only. Can we provide a sample policy snippet?
marco_eng: Sample routing header we use:
```
X-Redwood-Routing: {"region_preference":"eu-west-1","failover_regions":["eu-central-1"],"allow_control_plane":false}
```
Note: control plane false will reduce telemetry and some analytics.
lena_se: Can we confirm SLA impact? If control plane disabled, some rollback/alerting features might be unavailable. Need to surface this to customer.
omar_ops: SLA for Dedicated remains the same for serving path. Observability retention and some traces will be limited if telemetry is routed out. We should call that out.
priya_privacy: For BYOK: we support customer-managed keys via KMS in eu-west-1. For on-prem HSM, we need an enterprise engagement. Also confirm key escrow policy — we do not hold plaintext keys.
sam_sales: Great. Pricing: can we give a quick back-of-envelope for monthly reserved capacity to hit 300 rps with p95 120ms?
marco_eng: Rough calc: 300 rps * 120ms -> concurrency ~36. Assume per-GPU throughput ~120 tokens/s depending on model, need ~1-2 GPUs per shard. I’ll ask infra to model exact GPU count with quantization profile.
lena_se: I'll prepare a short customer-facing brief: architecture diagram, routing policy sample, subprocessor list (EU-only), BYOK checklist, and pricing placeholders.
infra-bot: Deploy requested: create eu-only telemetry toggle ticket #INC-5421 (assigned to marco_eng).
marco_eng: Filed INC-5421, ETA for toggle: 4 business days. Also starting capacity model; will attach numbers here.
sam_sales: Thanks — can Priya draft the attestation template and legal addendum we can ship?
priya_privacy: Yes, I’ll draft and loop in legal. Expect a draft in 2 business days.
sam_sales: Perfect. Next steps: Lena to send brief + pricing; Marco to attach capacity numbers; Priya to draft attestation. I’ll update QuantHealth and reconvene after docs. :thumbsup:
